title: a-requester-takes-its-reply
intention: Bus.request (cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:444), when it returns the reply correlated to the envelope it posted, writes that reply's delivery receipt through record_delivery (to=the requester, by=the requester) unless the reply already has one. So a reply that its requester read in hand no longer stands in undelivered() forever. The standing pile of such replies is drained once.
why: 2791 of 3181 undelivered envelopes are trouble->cairn replies the cairn device already read through Bus.request; the operator's undelivered count cannot show the mail nobody took while they stand
traces_to: Law 7 (the undelivered count is a diagnostic surface; 2,791 answered replies drown the few envelopes nobody took); ticket 7cb1989e7825 (mail arrives, and what cannot marks itself); RULE 1 (the fix lives in the bus's own request(), the door every requester already uses).
how: Measured 2026-10-02 by BusDevice().undelivered(limit=100000): 3181 undelivered personal envelopes, dated 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-02. 2791 are trouble->cairn, all with body {troubles: [...]}, why 'live reply', each with a reply_to. They are the answers to cairn/devices/cairn/device.py:97, where the cairn device's trouble pane calls self._bus.request(sender=cairn, to='trouble', verb='live'). The trouble shim's deliver (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:747) posts the handler's dict back as a personal '<verb> reply'. Bus.request reads it from the ring or the store and returns it, but never calls record_delivery (bus.py:503), so the store's anti-join (sql_missing_receipt, bus.py:485) reports it undelivered forever. 'cairn' has no wired delivery hook, so nothing else ever takes it. Of the rest: 378 codemother->tester 'sealed reply' answer tester/cli.py:327, a post() and not a request(). That half is ticket cff5a197b3c4 (the tester takes its reply, TICKETME), not this one. 9 to harbor_master; 1 each to charter, press_office, and cairn from operator_inbox. Build: in Bus.request, on each return path (ring hit, store hit, poll hit), call self.record_delivery(reply['id'], to=sender, by=sender) if reply['id'] is not in self._ring_delivered. The receipt flushes with the next beat's flush() like every other one. A reply already delivered by a wired hook during post's poke chain (codemother, web_server) keeps its one receipt. One-time drain: a scratchpad script reads undelivered(to='cairn') and records delivery for each envelope whose sender is 'trouble' and that carries a reply_to (by='drain-a-requester-takes-its-reply'), flushes, and puts the count on the verdict. The bus store is instance-space.
falsifier: RED if: (1) under a scratch bus with a fixture device wired to answer a verb, after bus.request returns its reply and bus.flush() runs, undelivered(to=<requester>) still holds that reply; (2) after the same exchange the delivery table holds more than one receipt for the reply envelope when the requester also had a wired delivery hook (a double receipt); (3) a reply that request() did NOT return (an envelope posted to the requester with no request open) is marked delivered by the exchange. WRONG INTENT if a reply read through request() must stay available to a second reader as undelivered mail. Horizon: the tester seal of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_requester_takes_its_reply.py.
watchme: none, because the proof beside cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py (test_a_requester_takes_its_reply, under ticket 7cb1989e7825) reds at every reseal if request() stops receipting, and the operator's undelivered count is read at every session open
children: none, because the receipt in request() and the one-time drain are one build in the bus
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Where? cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py:444, Bus.request, on each of its three return paths. (2) What call? self.record_delivery(reply['id'], to=sender, by=sender), guarded by reply['id'] not in self._ring_delivered. (3) Proof? cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_requester_takes_its_reply.py, PROVES keys 1-3, red first, under BusDevice.scratch.

chart_claim.filled_by: CC chart chain (orient f05a6d770bc7 .. validate 229acb966e74, each learned)

decisions.text: D1 THE RECEIPT: in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py, Bus.request gains one private helper, _taken(self, reply, sender), which calls self.record_delivery(reply['id'], to=sender, by=sender) when reply['id'] is not in self._ring_delivered, and returns reply. Each of request's three return statements (the ring hit `return ring_replies[0]`, the store hit `return replies[0]` before the loop, and the poll hit `return replies[0]` inside the loop) becomes `return self._taken(<that reply>, sender)`. Nothing else in request changes; its timeout path still raises.

D2 THE DOCSTRING: Bus.request's docstring gains one paragraph: the reply request() returns is in the requester's hand, so request() writes its receipt (ticket 6b1e13704e17; measured 2026-10-02, 2791 trouble->cairn replies stood undelivered because nothing receipted them), unless the poke chain already receipted it for a wired requester, which the _ring_delivered guard reads.

D3 WHY THE RING GUARD SUFFICES: a wired requester's hook receipts the reply inside post()'s poke chain, which completes before post() returns to request(), so the reply id is in _ring_delivered when request() reads it; flush() clears the ring only on the beat, never inside request(). A receipt for a reply first read from the store after a flush is a new receipt for mail no hook took.

D4 THE DRAIN, once, after the build commit and before the seal: a scratchpad script builds BusDevice(), reads undelivered(to='cairn', limit=100000), and for each envelope whose sender is 'trouble' and whose reply_to is set, calls record_delivery(env['id'], to='cairn', by='drain-a-requester-takes-its-reply'); then flush(). It prints the count drained and the undelivered census by (sender, addressee) after, and the count is appended to cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/history.json through the record door (cairn artifact write --verb append). Nothing else is drained: the tester's 378 belong to ticket cff5a197b3c4.

D5 PROOF: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_requester_takes_its_reply.py, PROVES keys 1-3 as committed red at 061e6d72 (teeth 1 and 3 red, tooth 2 the green double-receipt guard). It is not edited by the build.
